title: Child health and well visits
summary: Describes what to expect at well-child visits from birth to age 10, including screenings, vaccines, developmental milestones and coverage.

assets.alt: Child and doctor at a well visit

atoms.title: Why well-child visits matter
atoms.question: Why are well-child visits important?
atoms.text: Regular wellness checks, screenings and tests help support a child's health and track development so parents can understand how to help as the child grows. Well-child visits help keep up with fast growth to make sure it is healthy and on track. Topics include vaccines, screenings for each stage of development, and when to schedule regular preventive care visits.

atoms.title: Are child well visits covered?
atoms.question: Are child well visits covered by insurance?
atoms.text: Most health insurance plans are required to cover preventive care, which includes child well visits. As long as your child sees a network provider and the visit only covers preventive care, these visits will not cost you anything out of pocket. Most health plans cover early child well visits or provide assistance, so call the number on your insurance card for more information.

atoms.title: Vaccines at well-child visits
atoms.question: How do vaccines work at well-child visits?
atoms.text: During a well-child visit, your child's care provider explains which vaccines your child is able to get. Vaccines may help reduce the risk of infection by working with the body's natural defenses to safely develop immunity to disease. Some vaccines, like a flu shot, may be recommended yearly, while others are recommended based on age.

atoms.title: Screenings and milestones from birth to 24 months
atoms.question: What happens at well-child visits from birth to 24 months?
atoms.text: Visits in the first 2 years happen fairly often. Birth to 6 months includes hearing, vision and blood screenings, with milestones like social smile, cooing and rolling over. At 9 to 15 months, screenings add anemia and lead, and milestones include standing or walking and starting to talk. At 18 to 24 months, autism screening is added, with milestones like climbing and using a fork or spoon.

atoms.title: Screenings and milestones from ages 2 to 4
atoms.question: What happens at well-child visits from ages 2 to 4?
atoms.text: Well-child visits for ages 2 to 4 follow an annual schedule. At 2 and 2 1/2 years, screenings include hearing, vision, autism or development, oral health, and anemia and tuberculosis for high-risk children. At 3 and 4 years, screenings include hearing, vision, oral health and development. Milestones include using phrases at 3 and dressing themselves and identifying emotions at 4.

atoms.title: Screenings and milestones from ages 5 to 10
atoms.question: What happens at well-child visits from ages 5 to 10?
atoms.text: At age 5, screenings include hearing, vision, oral health and development. From ages 6 through 10, screenings include hearing, vision, oral health and behavioral, social and emotional screenings. Every visit includes a physical exam, vaccines, and height, weight and BMI. Providers discuss topics such as physical activity, eating habits, safe media use, puberty and drug and alcohol awareness.

When do behavioral screenings start for kids?

atoms.title: Safety topics at well visits to age 4
atoms.question: What topics do providers discuss at early well-child visits?
atoms.text: From birth to 24 months, providers discuss topics like sleep habits, hygiene, car seats, when to start solid foods, nutrition, child care, infant CPR, dental checks, child-proofing, sun protection, water safety, potty training and screen time. From ages 2 to 4, topics include school readiness, injury prevention, food security and a safe environment.

atoms.title: Preventive care checklists for children
atoms.question: Where can I find a well-visit checklist for my child?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare offers a child well visit checklist to help parents prepare and have a more helpful appointment. Checklists for preventive care visits are available for every age, from 1 month to adulthood. Making preventive visits part of your family's routine can set your child up for success in their own health care journey.

atoms.title: Healthy First Steps for Community Plan families
atoms.question: How does Healthy First Steps help with child well visits?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Community Plan members may have access to the Healthy First Steps program, which can help find a care provider, schedule well-child visits and connect with educational and community resources. To get started, call 1-800-599-5985, TTY 711, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The program is only available in certain states.

atoms.title: Help with transportation and food
atoms.question: What if I need help getting to appointments or getting food?
atoms.text: If you need help getting to an appointment, or getting formula or healthy food, call the number on your insurance card. If you are having a hard time getting food or are experiencing unemployment, your care provider may be able to connect you with resources that can help.
